question: A 7-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents for the evaluation of pubic hair development. She has a history of a fracture in each leg and one fracture in her right arm. Her performance at school is good. There is no family history of serious illness. She takes no medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. Genital examination shows coarse, dark hair along the labia. The breast glands are enlarged and the breast bud extends beyond the areolar diameter. There are several hyperpigmented macules with rough, serpiginous borders of different sizes on the lower and upper extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Early onset of pubic hair development" -> "Enlarged breast glands with breast bud extending beyond areolar diameter" -> "Hyperpigmented macules with rough, serpiginous borders on extremities" -> "Possible precocious puberty" -> 80%
CHAIN: "History of multiple fractures" -> "Coarse, dark hair along the labia" -> "Enlarged breast glands" -> "Hyperpigmented macules on extremities" -> "Possible McCune-Albright syndrome" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 7-year-old girl with early onset of pubic hair development, enlarged breast glands, hyperpigmented macules on extremities, and a history of fractures is McCune-Albright syndrome. This is supported by the presence of coarse, dark hair along the labia, which is a characteristic feature of this syndrome. The evidence path linking limb structure to symptoms associated with Albright's Syndrome further supports this diagnosis.
analysis: The constellation of symptoms including early onset of pubic hair development, enlarged breast glands, hyperpigmented macules on extremities, and a history of fractures in a 7-year-old girl is highly suggestive of McCune-Albright syndrome. This syndrome is characterized by the presence of polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots, and precocious puberty. The presence of coarse, dark hair along the labia further supports this diagnosis. Osteogenesis imperfecta typically presents with multiple fractures but does not typically involve precocious puberty or hyperpigmented macules. Neurofibromatosis type I and tuberous sclerosis do not typically present with the combination of symptoms described. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia can present with precocious puberty but does not typically involve the skeletal findings seen in this case.
